findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple chemical sanitizers to not meet required chemical sanitizing concentrations:
1) The dish machine at the bar (0 ppm Cl). CORRECTED- sanitizer was replaced, machine was primed, and ran until it was observed to be in compliance.
2) The sanitizer bucket was observed at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- the bucket was remade to 200 ppm.
Ensure chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces are tested at a frequency to ensure the concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label (50-200 ppm Chlorine, and 200-400 ppm quaternary ammonia).
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A). [P]

findings.comment: Inspector observed a gallon of milk held past it’s expiration date (6/9/26). CORRECTED- the milk was voluntarily discarded. Ensure prepackaged foods are not held past their expiration or “best by” dates to prevent the growth of pathogens.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
3-501.15 Two pans full to the top with cheese sauce prepared during the morning shift were observed sitting on the prep table cooling. Surface and internal temperatures were at 90F/100F and 107F/108F respectively. Cheese sauce was held on the stove in a double boiler until removed for cooling around 130p based on information provided. Temperature was not checked at any point during the process. Cook had ~20 minutes to get product below 70F per the time frame indicated. Cheese sauce was portioned into four pans to allow for shallower amount of product in each pan, and pans were placed in a freezer to flash chill the product. Methods for proper cooling were discussed, and cook was advised to monitor the temperature during cooling to ensure foods are cooling quickly and properly. 
Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the following time and temperature criteria: 135F to 70F/below in 2hrs and 70F to 41F/below in additional 4hrs (total cooling time must not exceed 6hrs). One or more of the following methods shall be used to cool foods based on the type of food being cooled: (1)place food in shallow pans; (2) separate food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) use rapid cooling equipment; (4) stir food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) use containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) add ice as an ingredient (when applicable); and/or (7) other effective methods. When placed in cooling or cold holding equipment, food containers in which food is being cooled shall be arranged to provide maximum heat transfer through the container walls and loosely covered, or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination during the cooling period to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food.

Clean the floor under the fryers.  *Note: the fryers do not easily move due to rollers on fryers not rolling properly, so the floor may need to be cleaned as well as possible with the fryers in place.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750.540a: Absence of an IL Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager (FSSMC) on duty at time of inspection.  Employee present has an expired license and will be taking an online course soon.  A FSSMC shall be on duty at all times when there is food being prepared or served.  A follow-up inspection will be conducted in 90 days to verify a FSSMC is on duty during preparation and service of food, unless once the certificate from the IL Dept of Public Health is received, the inspector is notified, April at 535-3100 or email at aprilc@co.sangamon.il.us with the certified person's name, certificate ID #, and the expiration date.  If this is received prior to follow-up date and the inspector is notified, a follow-up inspection will not be necessary, therefore saving a follow-up inspection fee.
